subject: Combination plot: bar + line plot with their respective y-axis on  opposite sides

messages.author: 901675ac81696523
messages.subject: Combination plot: bar + line plot with their respective y-axis on  opposite sides
parts:
I was wondering if ggplot2 can do something like this:

http://users.fmg.uva.nl/rgrasman/rpages/2005/08/combination-plot-bar-line-plot-with_05.html

I found their method a bit convoluted but couldn't find anything
similar in the ggplot book of plotting separate datasets with
different scales on the same graph. Addition of geom_errorbar would
also be nice.

Thanks,

Shane

Hadley has probably a better answer, but I think the answer is no.

The big problem is : "plot with their respective y-axis on opposite sides". See here : http://tolstoy.newcastle.edu.au/R/e5/help/08/11/7405.html

"Unfortunately, the capability is currently unavailable in ggplot2 and is unlikely to ever be available because I believe it is a fundamentally inaccurate means of presenting data. However, in the next version it will be much easier to created faceted displays with varying scales, which should be a better solution for many of these types of problems. "

David

> "Unfortunately, the capability is currently unavailable in ggplot2 and is
> unlikely to ever be available because I believe it is a fundamentally
> inaccurate means of presenting data. However, in the next version it will be
> much easier to created faceted displays with varying scales, which should be
> a better solution for many of these types of problems. "

Exactly right :) However, that's not actually needed for this chart:
note that the scales hardly overlap so you don't lose anything but
having two separate plots on top of each other.

# Restructure data into a single data frame
RT = matrix(c(814, 500, 424, 394, 967, 574, 472, 446),4,2)
colnames(RT) = c('repetition','alternation')
rownames(RT) = c('7-yrs','11-yrs','15-yrs','21-yrs')

library(ggplot2)
rt <- melt(RT)
names(rt) <- c("age", "trt", "value")
rt$variable <- "rt"

errors <- melt(as.matrix(error))
names(errors) <- c("age", "trt", "value")
errors$variable <- "error"

df <- rbind(rt, errors)

# Make sure factors are ordered correctly
df$age <- factor(df$age, levels = c("7-yrs", "11-yrs", "15-yrs", "21-yrs"))

# Which results in:
structure(list(age = structure(c(1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 1L, 2L, 3L,
4L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L), .Label = c("7-yrs", "11-yrs",
"15-yrs", "21-yrs"), class = "factor"), trt = structure(c(2L,
2L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L), .Label =
c("alternation",
"repetition"), class = "factor"), value = c(814, 500, 424, 394,
967, 574, 472, 446, 10, 6, 6, 4, 13, 7, 6, 3), variable = c("rt",
"rt", "rt", "rt", "rt", "rt", "rt", "rt", "error", "error", "error",
"error", "error", "error", "error", "error")), .Names = c("age",
"trt", "value", "variable"), row.names = c(NA, 16L), class = "data.frame")

# It's now straightforward to create recreate the plot with lines
# or with bars:

plot <- ggplot(df, aes(age, value, colour = trt, fill = trt)) +
facet_grid(variable ~ . , scale = "free")

plot + geom_bar(position = "dodge")
plot + geom_line(aes(group = trt)) + geom_point()

# It's then just a matter of combining the two:
plot +
geom_bar(position = "dodge", data = subset(df, variable == "rt")) +
geom_line(aes(group = trt), data = subset(df, variable == "error"))
# Unfortunately this currently results in an error, which
# I've added to my to do list to fix


--
